info.title: nCino eVault
info.description: All routes are currently in development and should be treated as such.

servers.description: Token endpoint host (served at the domain root, not under /api)

post.summary: Generate or refresh an auth token
post.description: Exchanges API client credentials for a JWT access token. Authenticate with HTTP Basic using your client_id (username) and client_secret (password). Use grant_type `authorization_code` with the `code` issued for your <Glossary>OrgApiClient</Glossary> to obtain the first token, or grant_type `refresh_token` with a previously issued <Glossary>refresh token</Glossary> to renew one. The returned `access_token` is used as the Bearer token on all other endpoints.

get.description: Lightweight connection/health check. Requires a valid <Glossary>bearer token</Glossary> but no specific permission — a 200 response confirms the caller's credentials are valid and can reach the eVault API. No environment segment or identifiers are needed.

post.description: Creates a new <Glossary>eNote</Glossary> in eVault from the supplied borrower, property, and loan details along with the eNote document data (the eNote file and its PDF rendering).

parameters.name: environment
parameters.description: The environment where the eNote, transaction, or audit log will be located.

requestBody.description: In order to create an eNote, all of the following must be included in the request body

get.description: Retrieves the full details and current status of an <Glossary>eNote</Glossary> by its guid, including its registration status, named parties, and <Glossary>audit log</Glossary> entries.

parameters.name: enote_id
parameters.description: The unique identifier for an eNote

get.description: Retrieves the <Glossary>smartdoc</Glossary> (SMART Doc®) representation of an <Glossary>eNote</Glossary> by its guid.
Retrieves the PDF rendering of an <Glossary>eNote</Glossary> by its guid.

Retrieves the <Glossary>audit log</Glossary> for an <Glossary>eNote</Glossary> — the time-ordered record of events (registration, transfers, status changes, and so on) recorded against its <Glossary>electronic record</Glossary>.

requestBody.description: In order to upload documents to an eNote, all of the following must be included in the request body

get.description: Retrieves a single <Glossary>audit log</Glossary> entry by its guid.

parameters.name: audit_log_id
parameters.description: The unique identifier for an audit log

get.description: Retrieves a previously submitted transaction by its transaction guid, including its current status and details.

parameters.name: transaction_id
parameters.description: The unique identifier for a transaction

post.description: Confirms or updates a pending transaction — for example accepting or rejecting a pending <Glossary>transfer</Glossary> awaiting confirmation. The confirmation type is specified in the request body.

requestBody.description: In order to perform this transaction, include the following in the request body

post.description: Looks up the current registry state of an <Glossary>eNote</Glossary> by its <Glossary>MIN</Glossary> or eNote guid, returning status or summary information.

requestBody.description: In order to perform an inquiry, all of the following must be included in the request body

post.description: Verifies connectivity to <Glossary>MERS eRegistry</Glossary> or <Glossary>MERS eDelivery</Glossary> for the given environment. The target is set by the address type in the request body.

requestBody.description: In order to perform a connectivity test, all of the following must be included in the request body

post.description: Registers a newly created <Glossary>eNote</Glossary> on <Glossary>MERS eRegistry</Glossary>, establishing the initial <Glossary>controller</Glossary> and the <Glossary>location</Glossary> that maintains its <Glossary>authoritative copy</Glossary>. On success the eNote's <Glossary>electronic record</Glossary> is created with a status of Active.

requestBody.description: In order to perform a registration, all of the following must be included in the request body

post.description: Changes the lifecycle status of a registered <Glossary>eNote</Glossary>'s <Glossary>electronic record</Glossary> — for example marking it paid off, charged off, <Glossary>converted to paper</Glossary>, or <Glossary>paper replacement</Glossary>, or reversing a prior status change. The status type is specified in the request body.

requestBody.description: In order to perform a change status, all of the following must be included in the request body

post.description: Updates data or party associations on a registered <Glossary>eNote</Glossary>'s <Glossary>electronic record</Glossary> without a full transfer — for example adding or releasing a <Glossary>secured party</Glossary>, changing the <Glossary>master servicer</Glossary> or <Glossary>subservicer</Glossary>, or reporting a modification or assumption. The change type is specified in the request body.

requestBody.description: In order to perform a change data, all of the following must be included in the request body

post.description: Delivers the <Glossary>eNote</Glossary> to one or more recipient organizations via <Glossary>MERS eDelivery</Glossary>. Each recipient is identified by its <Glossary>MERS Org ID</Glossary> and may accept or reject the delivery.

requestBody.description: In order to perform a delivery, all of the following must be included in the request body

post.description: Changes the parties on a registered <Glossary>eNote</Glossary> — for example the <Glossary>controller</Glossary>, <Glossary>location</Glossary>, or <Glossary>secured party</Glossary>. The transfer type included in the request body determines which parties change.

requestBody.description: In order to perform a transfer, all of the following must be included in the request body

put.description: Creates a <Glossary>webhook</Glossary> — a URL eVault calls when subscribed <Glossary>webhook event</Glossary>s fire — with its <Glossary>signing key</Glossary> and the set of events it subscribes to.

requestBody.description: In order to create a webhook configuration, all of the following must be included in the request body

get.description: Retrieves a <Glossary>webhook</Glossary> configuration, including the <Glossary>webhook event</Glossary>s it subscribes to.

parameters.name: webhook_id
parameters.description: The unique identifier for a webhook configuration

post.description: Updates an existing <Glossary>webhook</Glossary> configuration's name, URL, <Glossary>signing key</Glossary>, enabled state, or subscribed events.

requestBody.description: All fields are optional; only the fields included in the request body are updated. The nCino webhook configuration cannot be edited.

post.summary: Update a webhook configuration's active status

requestBody.description: Enables or disables the webhook configuration

post.description: Sends a test event to a <Glossary>webhook</Glossary>'s configured URL and reports whether delivery succeeded.

200.description: Sends a test event to the configured URL and returns whether it succeeded

post.description: When a subscribed event fires, eVault sends a POST to the `url` configured on the <Glossary>webhook</Glossary>. Every event uses the same payload shape; the `event_type` field identifies which event fired and the identifier fields present depend on the event (see the schema). Verify the `ncino-evault-signature` header to confirm the payload's authenticity.

parameters.name: ncino-evault-signature
parameters.description: Base64-encoded HMAC-SHA256 signature of the raw request body, computed with the signing key configured on the webhook. Use it to verify the payload came from eVault and was not modified in transit.

bearerAuth.description: JWT access token used to authorize every API request. Send it as `Authorization: Bearer <access_token>`. Tokens are issued by the token endpoint (POST https://evault.ncino.com/oauth/auth_token) and expire after the `expires_in` seconds returned there (default 3600); request a new token or exchange the refresh token once it expires.

basicAuth.description: HTTP Basic credentials used only by the token endpoint (POST /oauth/auth_token). The username is your API client_id and the password is your client_secret, sent as `Authorization: Basic base64(client_id:client_secret)`.

enote_guid.description: Alternative to min. Either min or enote_guid is required.

approvalDescription.example: signature doesn't match the value on mers registry
signature doesn't match the value on mers registry

example.approvalDescription: signature doesn't match the value on mers registry

grant_type.description: The OAuth2 grant type being used.

code.description: Required when grant_type is `authorization_code`. The authorization code issued for your org API client (returned as `clientId`/`id` when the API client was authorized for the org).

refresh_token.description: Required when grant_type is `refresh_token`. A refresh token returned by a previous token request.

access_token.description: JWT bearer token to send as `Authorization: Bearer <access_token>` on API requests.

expires_in.description: Lifetime of the access token in seconds.

refresh_token.description: Token used to obtain a new access token without re-sending credentials.

key.description: A webhook event you can subscribe to, used as the `key` of each entry in a webhook configuration's `events` array (enable an event by setting its `value` to true). A parent key (for example `change_data`, `change_status`, `connectivity`, `delivery`, `inquiry`, `registration`, `transfer`) enables every event in that group.

value.description: Whether this event type is enabled for the webhook configuration.

signingKey.description: Secret key used to sign webhook payloads so receivers can verify their authenticity.

sendEmailOnError.description: When true, an email is sent if the webhook fails to deliver.

isTest.description: When true, the configuration targets the test (stage) environment.

edit_webhook_configuration_post.description: All fields are optional; only the fields included in the request body are updated.

webhook_event_type.description: The event that fired, sent as the `event_type` field of the webhook payload. Values are the lowercased event keys. Subscribe to the events you want to receive via the `events` array when creating or editing a webhook configuration. A parent key (for example `change_data`, `change_status`, `connectivity`, `delivery`, `inquiry`, `registration`, `transfer`) can be subscribed to on its own to receive every event in that group.

webhook_event_callback_message.description: Payload eVault sends as a POST to the configured webhook URL when a subscribed event fires. `org_id` and `event_type` are always present; the remaining identifier fields are included only when they are relevant to the event that fired. The body is signed — verify it using the `ncino-evault-signature` header (see the parameter on this callback).

org_id.description: The guid of the org the event belongs to. Always present.

enote_id.description: Included when the event relates to an eNote.

transaction_id.description: Included when the event relates to a MERS transaction.

audit_log_id.description: Included when the event has an associated audit log.

document_id.description: Included when the event relates to a document.

api_client_id.description: Included when the event relates to an API client.

org_api_client.description: Included when the event relates to an org API client.

user_id.description: Included when the event was initiated by a user.

additional_info.description: Optional event-specific context. Included only when the event carries extra detail.
